title: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education - National Value Education - Negative Behaviour
exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
subject: National Value Education

questions.q: In Civic Education, **Negative Behaviour** is best described as:
options: Actions that strictly conform to the traditional rules of a nation
Any unacceptable, anti-social, or deviant action that violates societal values and norms
Behaviors that guarantee immediate financial prosperity for a family
Defending human rights through legal constitutional protests
questions.explain: **Negative Behaviour** refers to actions that go against the accepted norms, rules, and moral values of a society, often causing harm to the individual and the community.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: Which of the following scenarios is a clear example of **Ostentatious Living**, which is classified as a negative behaviour?
options: A wealthy businessman secretly donating millions to an orphanage
A politician using public funds to throw an extremely lavish, public party just to show off his wealth to neighbors
A teacher saving her salary for five years to build a modest house
A student working two jobs to afford necessary university textbooks
questions.explain: **Ostentatious living** is the deliberate, showy, and excessive display of wealth or luxury intended to attract attention, cause envy, or flaunt status, often at the expense of modesty and sometimes funded illegally.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: An excessive love for money usually drives individuals to commit various anti-social acts. Which of the following negative behaviors is predominantly driven by this factor?
options: Regularity at a low-paying government job
Drug trafficking and fraudulent practices
Total adherence to the rule of law
Engaging in voluntary community service
questions.explain: The **excessive love of money** often pushes individuals into desperate, illegal means of acquiring wealth, such as **drug trafficking**, robbery, and financial fraud.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: Examination malpractice is a widely condemned negative behavior. What is a direct long-term effect of unchecked examination malpractice on a nation?
options: It significantly boosts the nation's international academic reputation
It produces a highly skilled, intelligent workforce
It causes high inefficiency as unqualified individuals eventually occupy professional positions
It drastically reduces the national crime rate
questions.explain: When students cheat their way through school (**examination malpractice**), they graduate without actual knowledge. This causes massive **inefficiency** when these unqualified people enter the workforce.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: Cultism and drug trafficking generally lead to which specific effect on a society?
options: Total eradication of corruption
A very high crime rate and social insecurity
Perfect harmony among the youth
Massive improvements in democratic institutions
questions.explain: Negative behaviors such as **cultism** and **drug trafficking** inherently involve violence, illegal arms, and substance abuse, directly resulting in a **high crime rate**.

questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: Which of the following is the most effective strategy for **promoting positive behaviour** among the youth in a society?
options: Publicly rewarding hard work, honesty, and academic excellence
Ignoring minor offenses committed by wealthy citizens
Encouraging a total disregard for time (African time)
Promoting underage voting during local elections
questions.explain: Recognizing and **rewarding positive acts** like honesty and excellence serves as a powerful motivation for youths to emulate those positive behaviors, thus combating value disorientation.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: Identify the negative behaviour defined as: 'The intentional failure to keep to agreed schedules or appointments, often casually excused as a cultural norm.'
options: Examination malpractice
Cultism
Disregard for time
Ostentatious living
questions.explain: **Disregard for time** (sometimes colloquially called 'African time') is a negative behavior where individuals fail to respect schedules, leading to massive inefficiency and unproductivity.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: Widespread negative behaviours such as corruption, drug trafficking, and ostentatious living invariably lead to **Value Disorientation** in a country. What does value disorientation mean?
options: A situation where good morals are abandoned and negative acts are celebrated as the new normal
The total integration of foreign technologies into local schools
A positive change where youths embrace hard work and honesty
The constitutional process of registering a new political party
questions.explain: **Value Disorientation** occurs when a society loses its moral compass; unethical and negative behaviors (like fraud or corruption) become widely accepted, while traditional positive values are mocked or ignored.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: **Ostentatious living** is often fueled by the excessive love of money. How does this negative behavior predominantly impact the wider society?
options: It strongly encourages deep national unity among all economic classes
It drives massive industrial and agricultural productivity
It provokes dangerous envy and greed, often pushing struggling youths toward a high crime rate to acquire similar illicit wealth
It rapidly diminishes value disorientation
questions.explain: When individuals flaunt illegally acquired, massive wealth (**ostentatious living**), it creates toxic societal pressures. It fuels intense **envy** and normalizes the "get-rich-quick" syndrome, pushing others into crime to mimic that lifestyle.
